subject: User defined function-- can it be used as likelihood in the "model" block?

messages.author: 5e0a072a41164542
messages.subject: User defined function-- can it be used as likelihood in the "model" block?
parts:
If my understanding of "increment_log_prob" function is right, we should be able to write the model block by specifying the log likelihood distribution log[ f(y|theta) ] in "increment_log_prob" to replace the tilde version: y~ some defined distribution.

It would be very helpful if the distribution is complex or not fully built in Stan.

For my project, I have a likelihood which is a little bit complicated. R code is as follows:

ff1 <- function(Y.fail,Kamp.fail,Y.cen,Kamp.cen,beta) {
  b0 <-beta[1]
  b1 <-beta[2]
  s <-exp(beta[3])
  mu <-exp(beta[4])
  ss<-exp(beta[5])
  int=function(ii){
  b=function(b){
  u=b0+b1*log(Kamp.fail[ii]-b)
  Z1=dnorm(Y.fail[ii],mean=u,sd=s)*dweibull(b,scale=mu,shape=ss)
return(Z1)
}
return(integrate(b,lower = 0, upper =Kamp.fail[ii],stop.on.error=F)$value)
}
int.cen=function(ii){
  b=function(b){
  u=b0+b1*log(Kamp.cen[ii]-b)
  Z1=pnorm(Y.cen[ii],mean=u,sd=s)*dweibull(b,scale=mu,shape=ss)
return(Z1)
}
return(1-integrate(b,lower = 0, upper =Kamp.cen[ii],stop.on.error=F)$value)
}

log.l=sum(log(vapply(X=1:N.fail,int,FUN.VALUE=0)))+sum(log(vapply(X=1:N.cen,int.cen,FUN.VALUE=0)))
return(-log.l)
}

It has "sum" function and "integrate" function.  Since Stan doesn't have "integrate" function at this point, I can use other code ( by summing up hundreds of small pieces) to realize it.

I found that in User Manual 2.3, section 15, page 107, we can create user-defined functions, and put the function as a separate block in Stan code. 

My question is, can I define a function which returns the log likelihood log[ f(y|theta) ], and then put it into the model block as increment_log_prob( log[ f(y|theta) ] )  ?
How can I put the user_defined function into the model block?


As a simple example:

functions {
real user_defined(real mu, real<lower=0> sigma, real x) {
y <- -log(sigma)- square(x-mu)/(2*square(sigma));
return y;
}
}
...
model {
increment_log_prob(user_defined(mu, sigma, x));  // I don't think it works, but want to know how to do it 
}

I don't think it works, but want to know how to use the user defined function. Do we have examples that include user defined questions?


My aim is to take advantage of the likelihood I presented above, to let it run in Stan as the distribution of data given parameters f(y|theta).


I'll be super grateful for your time and comments.


Dora

parts:
On Jul 11, 2014, at 5:48 PM, Dora Zhou <zhou...@gmail.com> wrote:

> If my understanding of "increment_log_prob" function is right, we should be able to write the model block by specifying the log likelihood distribution log[ f(y|theta) ] in replace of the tilde version: y~ some defined distribution.

Correct --- as we try to make clear in the manual, the y ~ notation
is just a shorthand for increment_log_prob (and it also drops constants).
> It would be very helpful if the distribution is complex or not fully built in Stan.
That's the use case we give in the chapter on user-defined distributions :-)

>
> For my project, I have a likelihood which is a little bit complicated. R code is as follows:
>
> ff1 <- function(Y.fail,Kamp.fail,Y.cen,Kamp.cen,beta) {
> b0 <-beta[1]
> b1 <-beta[2]
> s <-exp(beta[3])
> mu <-exp(beta[4])
> ss<-exp(beta[5])
> int=function(ii){
> b=function(b){
> u=b0+b1*log(Kamp.fail[ii]-b)
> Z1=dnorm(Y.fail[ii],mean=u,sd=s)*dweibull(b,scale=mu,shape=ss)
> return(Z1)
> }
> return(integrate(b,lower = 0, upper =Kamp.fail[ii],stop.on.error=F)$value)
> }
> int.cen=function(ii){
> b=function(b){
> u=b0+b1*log(Kamp.cen[ii]-b)
> Z1=pnorm(Y.cen[ii],mean=u,sd=s)*dweibull(b,scale=mu,shape=ss)
> return(Z1)
> }
> return(1-integrate(b,lower = 0, upper =Kamp.cen[ii],stop.on.error=F)$value)
> }
>
> log.l=sum(log(vapply(X=1:N.fail,int,FUN.VALUE=0)))+sum(log(vapply(X=1:N.cen,int.cen,FUN.VALUE=0)))
> return(-log.l)
> }
>
> It has "sum" function and "integrate" function.

Stan has a sum() function, but not integrate().

> Since Stan doesn't "integrate" function at this point, I can use other code ( by summing up hundreds of small pieces) to realize it.

Now that gets complicated to code. The main issue is whether
Stan's automatically calculated derivatives will do the right
thing.

> I found that in User Manual 2.3, section 15, page 107, we can create user-defined functions, and put the function as a separate block in Stan code.
>
> My question is, can I define a function which returns the log likelihood log[ f(y|theta) ], and then put it into the model block as increment_log_prob( log[ f(y|theta) ] ) ?

Yes. You can also define your own densities and use
them with ~. The manual has examples.

Warning: we're still working out some kinks in the functions
and they don't recompile in R yet and there are some issues
with namespaces and voids and things being cleaned up.
> How can I put the user_defined function into the model block?
It'll work just like a built-in function.

> As a simple example:
>
> functions {
> real user_defined(real mu, real<lower=0> sigma, real x) {
> y <- -log(sigma)- square(x-mu)/(2*square(sigma));
> return y;
> }
> }
> ...
> model {
> increment_log_prob(user_defined(mu, sigma, x)); // I don't think it works, but want to know how to do it
> }
>
> I don't think it works, but want to know how to use the user defined function. Do we have examples that include user defined questions?

Yes, the above will work.

There aren't examples yet with user-defined functions.

If you had declared "user_defined" as "user_defined_log" then
you could've written the model as:

mu ~ user_defined(sigma,x);

- Bob

Hi Bob,

Thank you for your suggestions! Now I successfully run a toy model using user-defined function "dnorm":

##### Data ###
x=-49:50
e=rnorm(100)
y = 2 + x + e

toy_dat <- list(N=100, x=x, e=e, y = y )
toy_dat$y

#######################################################
######### Way 4. Use user-defined function ############

toy_code3 <- '
  functions {
    real dnorm_log(real x, real mu, real sigma){
    return -square(x-mu)/(2*square(sigma));
    } 
  }

  data {
    int<lower=0> N; 
    vector[N] y; 
    vector[N] x; 
  }

  parameters {
    real eta; 
    real mu0; 
    real mu1;
    real<lower=0> sigmasq;
  }

  transformed parameters {
    real<lower=0> sigma;
    real beta0;
    real beta1;
    sigma <- sqrt(sigmasq);
    beta0 <- mu0 + 10 * eta ;
    beta1 <- mu1 + 2 * eta ;
  }

  model {
    mu0 ~ dnorm(1, 1);
    mu1 ~ dnorm(1, 1);
    eta ~ dnorm(0, 1);
    sigmasq ~ inv_gamma(0.001, 0.001); 
    y ~ normal(beta0 + beta1*x, sigma);
  }
'

toy_fit3 <- stan(model_code = toy_code3, data = toy_dat, 
            iter = 1000, chains = 2)

And I got same result with the model using the "normal" built-in function.

However, I defined my normal function "dnorm" only for real numbers, but not for vectors.   I tried to define another function called "dnorm2", for vectors, in order to let my vector "y" in model block, also run by my user-defined function:

#######################################################
######### Way 5. Play around user-defined function ############

toy_code4 <- '
  functions {
    real dnorm1_log(real x1, real mu1, real sigma1){
      return -square(x1-mu1)/(2*square(sigma1));
    } 
    vector dnorm2_log(vector x2, vector mu2, real sigma2) {
      return -(dot_self(x2-mu2))/(2*square(sigma2));
    } 
     
  }

  data {
    int<lower=0> N; 
    vector[N] y; 
    vector[N] x; 
  }

  parameters {
    real eta; 
    real mu0; 
    real mu1;
    real<lower=0> sigmasq;
  }

  transformed parameters {
    real<lower=0> sigma;
    real beta0;
    real beta1;
    vector[N] mu;
    sigma <- sqrt(sigmasq);
    beta0 <- mu0 + 10 * eta ;
    beta1 <- mu1 + 2 * eta ;
  }

  model {
    mu0 ~ dnorm1(1, 1);
    mu1 ~ dnorm1(1, 1);
    eta ~ dnorm1(0, 1);
    sigmasq ~ inv_gamma(0.001, 0.001); 
    y ~ dnorm2(beta0 + beta1*x, sigma);
  }
'

toy_fit4 <- stan(model_code = toy_code4, data = toy_dat, 
            iter = 1000, chains = 2)



However, this time the model keeps giving me error as follows:

Parse Error.  Function system defined, name=dnorm1_log

LOCATION OF PARSING ERROR (line = 6, position = 5):

PARSED:


  functions {
    real dnorm1_log(real x1, real mu1, real sigma1){
      return -square(x1-mu1)/(2*square(sigma1));
    } 
    

EXPECTED: <eps> BUT FOUND: 

vector dnorm2_log(vector x2, vector mu2, real sigma2) {
      return -(dot_self(x2-mu2))/(2*square(sigma2));


I tried several ways that I think should work, but failed.  Can you explain to me how to define a vector user-defined function?  What is wrong in the above code?    Thanks!!

PS.  I found for the parameters of user-defined function, we cannot add constraints, like real<lower=0>, vector[N].  It seems we can only use parameters without any constraint: real x, vector y, things like that.


Dora

parts:
This is a bug in the current RStan version that only lets
you define a function once per session. It's already fixed on
our dev branch and will be fixed in the next RStan release (which
we hope to make this week).

- Bob
